tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## 4bdddc46-3b80-45ec-bc37-523e74d4fda6
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

135	def list_assets(q: str = "", moment: list[str] = Query(default=[]), category: list[str] = Query(default=[]),
136	                role: list[str] = Query(default=[]), rating: list[str] = Query(default=[]),
137	                risk: list[str] = Query(default=[]), kind: str = "", key_mode: str = "", root: str = "",
138	                ranked: bool = False, project: str = "", limit: int = 60, offset: int = 0,
139	                favorites: bool = False):
140	    if ranked and (moment or q or role):
141	        # same scorer the planner uses
142	        res = A.find(A.Query(moments=moment, roles=role, categories=category, text=q or None,
143	                             max_rating="explicit", max_risk="high", project=project or None, limit=limit,
144	                             favorites_only=favorites))
145	        for r in res:
146	            r.pop("abs_path", None)
147	        return {"total": len(res), "items": res}
148	    where, args = ["1=1"], []
149	    if q:
150	        terms = [t for t in "".join(c if c.isalnum() else " " for c in q).split() if t]
151	        if terms:
152	            ids = [r[0] for r in db().execute("SELECT id FROM assets_fts WHERE assets_fts MATCH ?",
153	                                              (" ".join(f'"{t}"*' for t in terms),))]
154	            where.append(f"id IN ({','.join('?' * len(ids))})" if ids else "0")
155	            args += ids
156	    for col, vals in (("category", category), ("content_rating", rating), ("copyright_risk", risk)):
157	        if vals:
158	            # untagged assets (no rating yet) stay visible instead of silently disappearing
159	            extra = " OR content_rating IS NULL" if col == "content_rating" else ""
160	            where.append(f"({col} IN ({','.join('?' * len(vals))}){extra})")
161	            args += vals
162	    for m in moment:
163	        where.append("moments LIKE ?")
164	        args.append(f'%"{m}"%')
165	    for ro in role:
166	        where.append("roles LIKE ?")
167	        args.append(f'%"{ro}"%')
168	    if kind:
169	        where.append("kind = ?")
170	        args.append(kind)
171	    if root:
172	        where.append("root = ?")
173	        args.append(root)
174	    if key_mode:
175	        where.append("key_mode = ?")
176	        args.append(key_mode)
177	    if favorites:
178	        where.append("favorite = 1")
179	    con = db()
180	    w = " AND ".join(where)
181	    total = con.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assets WHERE {w}", args).fetchone()[0]
182	    rows = con.execute(f"SELECT * FROM assets WHERE {w} ORDER BY category, title LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
183	                       args + [limit, offset]).fetchall()
184	    return {"total": total, "items": [row_out(r) for r in rows]}

308	@app.get("/api/projects/{slug}/timeline")
309	def timeline(slug: str):
310	    """EDL resolved into output time, grouped by track, for the timeline view."""
311	    p = inside(PROJECTS, slug)
312	    edl = read_json(p / "edit.json")
313	    if not edl:
314	        return {"duration": 0, "tracks": {}, "warnings": []}
315	    warnings: list[str] = []
316	
317	    def lookup(i):
318	        try:
319	            return A.get(i)
320	        except KeyError:
321	            warnings.append(f"unknown asset {i}")
322	            return None
323	    try:
324	        validate(edl)
325	        spans = build_spans(edl, lookup)
326	    except (EDLError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
327	        return {"duration": 0, "tracks": {}, "warnings": [f"EDL error: {e}"]}
328	    tracks: dict[str, list] = {"segments": [], "overlays": [], "text": [], "sfx": [], "music": [], "bleeps": [],
329	                               "zooms": []}
330	    t = 0.0
331	    for i, s in enumerate(edl["segments"]):
332	        d = seg_duration(s, lookup)
333	        tracks["segments"].append({"i": i, "start": t, "end": t + d, "type": s.get("type", "source"),
334	                                   "label": s.get("id") or s.get("asset") or f"seg{i}", "src_in": s.get("in"),
335	                                   "src_out": s.get("out"), "speed": s.get("speed", 1), "effects": s.get("effects", []),
336	                                   "mode": s.get("mode") or edl.get("mode", "funny")})
337	        for z in s.get("zoom", []) + [dict(x, shake=True) for x in s.get("shake", [])]:
338	            a = z["at"] if "at" in z else (z["src_at"] - s["in"]) / s.get("speed", 1)
339	            dz = z.get("dur") or (z.get("in", 0.12) + z.get("hold", 0.6) + z.get("out", 0.18))
340	            tracks["zooms"].append({"start": t + a, "end": t + min(a + dz, d),
341	                                    "label": "shake" if z.get("shake") else f"x{z.get('to', 1.3)}"})
342	        t += d
343	    total = t
344	
345	    def add(track, evs, default_dur, label_fn):
346	        for k, ev in enumerate(evs):
347	            at = resolve_time(ev, spans, warnings, f"{track}[{k}]") if ("at" in ev or "src_at" in ev) else 0.0
348	            if at is None:
349	                continue
350	            a = lookup(ev["asset"]) if ev.get("asset") else None
351	            dur = ev.get("dur") or (ev.get("until", total) - at if track == "music" else None) \
352	                or (a.get("tail_s") or a.get("duration_s") if a else None) or default_dur
353	            tracks[track].append({"k": k, "start": at, "end": min(total, at + dur), "label": label_fn(ev, a),
354	                                  "asset": ev.get("asset"), "thumb": a.get("thumb") if a else None})
355	    add("overlays", edl.get("overlays", []), 1.5, lambda e, a: f"{e['type']}: {(a or {}).get('title') or e.get('file')}")
356	    add("text", edl.get("text", []), 1.2, lambda e, a: e.get("text", ""))
357	    add("sfx", edl.get("audio", {}).get("sfx", []), 1.0, lambda e, a: (a or {}).get("title") or e.get("asset"))
358	    add("music", edl.get("audio", {}).get("music", []), total, lambda e, a: (a or {}).get("title") or e.get("asset"))
359	    add("bleeps", edl.get("audio", {}).get("bleeps", []), 0.4, lambda e, a: "bleep")
360	    return {"duration": total, "tracks": tracks, "warnings": warnings, "format": edl.get("format", "landscape")}

384	class Job:
385	    def __init__(self, slug: str, stage: str, cmd: list[str], cwd: Path):
386	        self.id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
387	        self.slug, self.stage, self.cmd, self.cwd = slug, stage, cmd, cwd
388	        self.status = "running"
389	        self.lines: list[str] = []
390	        self.started = time.time()
391	        self.ended: float | None = None
392	        self.rc: int | None = None
393	        self.proc: subprocess.Popen | None = None
394	        threading.Thread(target=self._run, daemon=True).start()
395	
396	    def _run(self):
397	        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1", PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8")
398	        try:
399	            self.proc = subprocess.Popen(self.cmd, cwd=self.cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
400	                                         text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", env=env)
401	            for line in self.proc.stdout:
402	                self.lines.append(line.rstrip())
403	                if len(self.lines) > 4000:
404	                    del self.lines[:1000]
405	            self.rc = self.proc.wait()
406	            self.status = "done" if self.rc == 0 else "failed"
407	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
408	            self.lines.append(f"!! {e}")
409	            self.status = "failed"
410	        self.ended = time.time()
411	
412	    def public(self, tail: int = 200) -> dict:
413	        return {"id": self.id, "slug": self.slug, "stage": self.stage, "status": self.status, "rc": self.rc,
414	                "started": self.started, "elapsed": round((self.ended or time.time()) - self.started, 1),
415	                "log": self.lines[-tail:]}

"""Browser-playable previews of the motion-graphics templates (for the studio UI's Motion graphics page).

For each template: render it in preview mode (landscape, default vars) via motion.render, composite the
alpha .mov over a Minecraft gameplay still, and write
    studio/motion/previews/<name>.mp4    h264 960x540 30fps, +0.5s tail so it loops cleanly
    studio/motion/previews/<name>.jpg    poster (mid-frame)
    studio/motion/previews/<name>.json   {"mov": "<cached .mov name>"}: the cache key
Templates are discovered from studio/motion/templates/ on every call (never a fixed list). A preview is
only rebuilt when motion.render returns a different .mov (i.e. the template, shared files or brand changed).

The gameplay still is extracted once from a project's game recording (test-clip-02 first) into
previews/_bg_<orientation>.jpg; with no recording available a dark checkerboard is generated instead.

CLI (from studio/):
    uv run python -m mcstudio.motion_previews [names...] [--missing] [--force]
    uv run python -m mcstudio.motion_previews --render NAME [--vars JSON] [--orientation O] [--preview]
        (used by the UI's render jobs: renders, makes a viewable mp4, prints "@@RESULT {json}")
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from . import motion
from .paths import PROJECTS, STUDIO

PREVIEWS = motion.MOTION / "previews"
RENDERS = PREVIEWS / "renders"          # viewable mp4 copies of UI render jobs
SIZES = {"landscape": (960, 540), "vertical": (540, 960)}
FPS = 30
TAIL_S = 0.5                            # transparent hold appended so hover loops breathe


def _run(cmd: list[str]) -> None:
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"ffmpeg failed ({r.returncode}): {' '.join(cmd[:6])} ...\n{r.stderr[-2000:]}")


def _probe_duration(p: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    try:
        return float(r.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return 0.0


def _game_sources() -> list[Path]:
    """Gameplay recordings referenced by projects, test-clip-02 first."""
    pjs = sorted(PROJECTS.glob("*/project.json"), key=lambda p: (p.parent.name != "test-clip-02", p.parent.name))
    out = []
    for pj in pjs:
        try:
            g = (json.loads(pj.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("sources") or {}).get("game", {}).get("file")
        except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            continue
        if g:
            f = Path(g) if Path(g).is_absolute() else pj.parent / g
            if f.exists() and f not in out:
                out.append(f)
    return out


def background(orientation: str = "landscape") -> Path:
    """Gameplay still (or checkerboard) sized for the orientation; extracted once and reused."""
    w, h = SIZES[orientation]
    out = PREVIEWS / f"_bg_{orientation}.jpg"
    if out.exists() and out.stat().st_size > 0:
        return out
    PREVIEWS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # cover-scale then centre-crop (vertical gets the middle of the landscape frame)
    vf = f"scale={w}:{h}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop={w}:{h},setsar=1"
    for src in _game_sources():
        dur = _probe_duration(src)
        at = dur * 0.4 if dur > 1 else 0
        try:
            _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-ss", f"{at:.2f}", "-i", str(src), "-frames:v", "1",
                  "-vf", vf, "-q:v", "3", str(out)])
            if out.exists() and out.stat().st_size > 0:
                return out
        except RuntimeError:
            continue
    # fallback: dark checkerboard
    _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"color=c=0x1f1f1f:s={w}x{h}", "-frames:v", "1",
          "-vf", "geq=lum='if(mod(floor(X/24)+floor(Y/24),2),42,31)':cb=128:cr=128", str(out)])
    return out


def composite(mov: Path, out_mp4: Path, orientation: str = "landscape", tail: float = TAIL_S) -> Path:
    """Alpha .mov over the gameplay still -> h264 yuv420p mp4 (faststart, no audio)."""
    w, h = SIZES[orientation]
    bg = background(orientation)
    out_mp4.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = out_mp4.with_name(out_mp4.stem + ".part.mp4")
    # single-frame bg looped by the loop *filter* (no -loop 1 input: that can stall ffmpeg 9's scheduler)
    fc = (f"[0:v]loop=loop=-1:size=1:start=0,setpts=N/{FPS}/TB,scale={w}:{h},setsar=1[b];"
          f"[1:v]fps={FPS},scale={w}:{h}:flags=lanczos,format=yuva420p"
          + (f",tpad=stop_mode=add:stop_duration={tail}:color=black@0" if tail > 0 else "") + "[o];"
          f"[b][o]overlay=shortest=1:format=auto,format=yuv420p[v]")
    _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", str(bg), "-i", str(mov), "-filter_complex", fc, "-map", "[v]",
          "-an", "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "22", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
          "-movflags", "+faststart", str(tmp)])
    tmp.replace(out_mp4)
    return out_mp4


def poster(mp4: Path, out_jpg: Path) -> Path:
    d = max(0.0, _probe_duration(mp4) - TAIL_S)
    _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-ss", f"{d * 0.5:.2f}", "-i", str(mp4), "-frames:v", "1",
          "-q:v", "3", str(out_jpg)])
    return out_jpg


def paths(name: str) -> dict:
    return {"mp4": PREVIEWS / f"{name}.mp4", "jpg": PREVIEWS / f"{name}.jpg", "meta": PREVIEWS / f"{name}.json"}


def has_preview(name: str) -> bool:
    p = paths(name)
    return p["mp4"].exists() and p["jpg"].exists()


def make(name: str, force: bool = False, log=print) -> dict:
    """Render (cached) + composite the preview for one template. Returns {"mp4", "jpg", "mov", "skipped"}."""
    m = motion._manifest(name)
    orientation = "landscape" if "landscape" in m["orientations"] else m["orientations"][0]
    p = paths(name)
    t0 = time.time()
    mov = motion.render(name, {}, orientation=orientation, preview=True, force=False)
    meta = {}
    try:
        meta = json.loads(p["meta"].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    if not force and has_preview(name) and meta.get("mov") == mov.name:
        return {"mp4": p["mp4"], "jpg": p["jpg"], "mov": mov, "skipped": True}
    composite(mov, p["mp4"], orientation)
    poster(p["mp4"], p["jpg"])
    p["meta"].write_text(json.dumps({"mov": mov.name, "orientation": orientation,
                                     "made": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")}), encoding="utf-8")
    log(f"[preview] {name}: {p['mp4'].name} ({time.time() - t0:.1f}s)")
    return {"mp4": p["mp4"], "jpg": p["jpg"], "mov": mov, "skipped": False}


def viewable(mov: Path, orientation: str) -> Path:
    """Browser-playable mp4 of a rendered .mov over the gameplay still (cached by the .mov name)."""
    out = RENDERS / f"{mov.stem}.mp4"
    if not out.exists() or out.stat().st_mtime < mov.stat().st_mtime:
        composite(mov, out, orientation, tail=0)
    return out


def rel_url(p: Path) -> str:
    """/media/studio/... URL (server.py serves studio/motion/**) with an mtime cache-buster."""
    rel = p.resolve().relative_to(STUDIO.resolve()).as_posix()
    return f"/media/studio/{rel}?v={int(p.stat().st_mtime)}"


def render_job(name: str, vars: dict, orientation: str, preview: bool, duration: float | None) -> dict:
    print(f"rendering {name} ({orientation}, {'preview 540p30' if preview else 'full 1080p60'}) ...", flush=True)
    t0 = time.time()
    mov = motion.render(name, vars, orientation=orientation, preview=preview, duration=duration)
    print(f"rendered {mov.name} in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s; making browser preview ...", flush=True)
    mp4 = viewable(mov, orientation)
    rel = mov.resolve().relative_to(STUDIO.resolve().parent).as_posix()
    return {"name": name, "orientation": orientation, "preview": preview,
            "vars": motion.resolve_vars(name, vars), "mov": rel, "mov_url": rel_url(mov),
            "mp4_url": rel_url(mp4), "size": mov.stat().st_size}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m mcstudio.motion_previews",
                                 description="Make browser previews of the motion templates.")
    ap.add_argument("names", nargs="*", help="templates (default: all)")
    ap.add_argument("--missing", action="store_true", help="only templates without a preview yet")
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="re-composite even if cached")
    ap.add_argument("--render", metavar="NAME", help="render one template with --vars (UI render job)")
    ap.add_argument("--vars", default="{}", help="JSON object of template vars (with --render)")
    ap.add_argument("--orientation", default="landscape", choices=list(SIZES))
    ap.add_argument("--preview", action="store_true", help="(with --render) 540p30 instead of full res")
    ap.add_argument("--duration", type=float, help="(with --render) stretchable templates only")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if not shutil.which("ffmpeg"):
        print("error: ffmpeg not on PATH", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if a.render:
        try:
            res = render_job(a.render, json.loads(a.vars or "{}"), a.orientation, a.preview, a.duration)
        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as e:
            print(f"error: {e}", flush=True)
            return 1
        print("@@RESULT " + json.dumps(res), flush=True)
        return 0

    names = a.names or [t["name"] for t in motion.list_templates()]
    if a.missing:
        names = [n for n in names if not has_preview(n)]
    if not names:
        print("all templates have previews")
        return 0
    fails = 0
    for i, n in enumerate(names, 1):
        print(f"[{i}/{len(names)}] {n} ...", flush=True)
        try:
            r = make(n, force=a.force)
            if r["skipped"]:
                print(f"[preview] {n}: up to date", flush=True)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep going through the other templates
            fails += 1
            print(f"[preview] {n}: FAILED: {e}", flush=True)
    print(f"done: {len(names) - fails} ok, {fails} failed", flush=True)
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"ffmpeg failed ({r.returncode}): {' '.join(cmd[:6])} ...\n{r.stderr[-2000:]}")


def _probe_duration(p: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    try:
        return float(r.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return 0.0


def _game_sources() -> list[Path]:
    """Gameplay recordings referenced by projects, test-clip-02 first."""
    pjs = sorted(PROJECTS.glob("*/project.json"), key=lambda p: (p.parent.name != "test-clip-02", p.parent.name))
    out = []
    for pj in pjs:
        try:
            g = (json.loads(pj.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("sources") or {}).get("game", {}).get("file")
        except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            continue
        if g:
            f = Path(g) if Path(g).is_absolute() else pj.parent / g
            if f.exists() and f not in out:
                out.append(f)
    return out


def background(orientation: str = "landscape") -> Path:
    """Gameplay still (or checkerboard) sized for the orientation; extracted once and reused."""
    w, h = SIZES[orientation]
    out = PREVIEWS / f"_bg_{orientation}.jpg"
    if out.exists() and out.stat().st_size > 0:
        return out
    PREVIEWS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # cover-scale then centre-crop (vertical gets the middle of the landscape frame)
    vf = f"scale={w}:{h}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop={w}:{h},setsar=1"
    for src in _game_sources():
        dur = _probe_duration(src)
        at = dur * 0.4 if dur > 1 else 0
        try:
            _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-ss", f"{at:.2f}", "-i", str(src), "-frames:v", "1",
                  "-vf", vf, "-q:v", "3", str(out)])
            if out.exists() and out.stat().st_size > 0:
                return out
        except RuntimeError:
            continue
    # fallback: dark checkerboard
    _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"color=c=0x1f1f1f:s={w}x{h}", "-frames:v", "1",
          "-vf", "geq=lum='if(mod(floor(X/24)+floor(Y/24),2),42,31)':cb=128:cr=128", str(out)])
    return out


def composite(mov: Path, out_mp4: Path, orientation: str = "landscape", tail: float = TAIL_S) -> Path:
    """Alpha .mov over the gameplay still -> h264 yuv420p mp4 (faststart, no audio)."""
    w, h = SIZES[orientation]
    bg = background(orientation)
    out_mp4.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = out_mp4.with_name(out_mp4.stem + ".part.mp4")
    # single-frame bg looped by the loop *filter* (no -loop 1 input: that can stall ffmpeg 9's scheduler)
    fc = (f"[0:v]loop=loop=-1:size=1:start=0,setpts=N/{FPS}/TB,scale={w}:{h},setsar=1[b];"
          f"[1:v]fps={FPS},scale={w}:{h}:flags=lanczos,format=yuva420p"
          + (f",tpad=stop_mode=add:stop_duration={tail}:color=black@0" if tail > 0 else "") + "[o];"
          f"[b][o]overlay=shortest=1:format=auto,format=yuv420p[v]")
    _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", str(bg), "-i", str(mov), "-filter_complex", fc, "-map", "[v]",
          "-an", "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "22", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
          "-movflags", "+faststart", str(tmp)])
    tmp.replace(out_mp4)
    return out_mp4


def poster(mp4: Path, out_jpg: Path) -> Path:
    d = max(0.0, _probe_duration(mp4) - TAIL_S)
    _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-ss", f"{d * 0.5:.2f}", "-i", str(mp4), "-frames:v", "1",
          "-q:v", "3", str(out_jpg)])
    return out_jpg


def paths(name: str) -> dict:
    return {"mp4": PREVIEWS / f"{name}.mp4", "jpg": PREVIEWS / f"{name}.jpg", "meta": PREVIEWS / f"{name}.json"}


def has_preview(name: str) -> bool:
    p = paths(name)
    return p["mp4"].exists() and p["jpg"].exists()


def make(name: str, force: bool = False, log=print) -> dict:
    """Render (cached) + composite the preview for one template. Returns {"mp4", "jpg", "mov", "skipped"}."""
    m = motion._manifest(name)
    orientation = "landscape" if "landscape" in m["orientations"] else m["orientations"][0]
    p = paths(name)
    t0 = time.time()
    mov = motion.render(name, {}, orientation=orientation, preview=True, force=False)
    meta = {}
    try:
        meta = json.loads(p["meta"].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    if not force and has_preview(name) and meta.get("mov") == mov.name:
        return {"mp4": p["mp4"], "jpg": p["jpg"], "mov": mov, "skipped": True}
    composite(mov, p["mp4"], orientation)
    poster(p["mp4"], p["jpg"])
    p["meta"].write_text(json.dumps({"mov": mov.name, "orientation": orientation,
                                     "made": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")}), encoding="utf-8")
    log(f"[preview] {name}: {p['mp4'].name} ({time.time() - t0:.1f}s)")
    return {"mp4": p["mp4"], "jpg": p["jpg"], "mov": mov, "skipped": False}


def viewable(mov: Path, orientation: str) -> Path:
    """Browser-playable mp4 of a rendered .mov over the gameplay still (cached by the .mov name)."""
    out = RENDERS / f"{mov.stem}.mp4"
    if not out.exists() or out.stat().st_mtime < mov.stat().st_mtime:
        composite(mov, out, orientation, tail=0)
    return out


def rel_url(p: Path) -> str:
    """/media/studio/... URL (server.py serves studio/motion/**) with an mtime cache-buster."""
    rel = p.resolve().relative_to(STUDIO.resolve()).as_posix()
    return f"/media/studio/{rel}?v={int(p.stat().st_mtime)}"


def render_job(name: str, vars: dict, orientation: str, preview: bool, duration: float | None) -> dict:
    print(f"rendering {name} ({orientation}, {'preview 540p30' if preview else 'full 1080p60'}) ...", flush=True)
    t0 = time.time()
    mov = motion.render(name, vars, orientation=orientation, preview=preview, duration=duration)
    print(f"rendered {mov.name} in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s; making browser preview ...", flush=True)
    mp4 = viewable(mov, orientation)
    rel = mov.resolve().relative_to(STUDIO.resolve().parent).as_posix()
    return {"name": name, "orientation": orientation, "preview": preview,
            "vars": motion.resolve_vars(name, vars), "mov": rel, "mov_url": rel_url(mov),
            "mp4_url": rel_url(mp4), "size": mov.stat().st_size}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m mcstudio.motion_previews",
                                 description="Make browser previews of the motion templates.")
    ap.add_argument("names", nargs="*", help="templates (default: all)")
    ap.add_argument("--missing", action="store_true", help="only templates without a preview yet")
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="re-composite even if cached")
    ap.add_argument("--render", metavar="NAME", help="render one template with --vars (UI render job)")
    ap.add_argument("--vars", default="{}", help="JSON object of template vars (with --render)")
    ap.add_argument("--orientation", default="landscape", choices=list(SIZES))
    ap.add_argument("--preview", action="store_true", help="(with --render) 540p30 instead of full res")
    ap.add_argument("--duration", type=float, help="(with --render) stretchable templates only")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if not shutil.which("ffmpeg"):
        print("error: ffmpeg not on PATH", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if a.render:
        try:
            res = render_job(a.render, json.loads(a.vars or "{}"), a.orientation, a.preview, a.duration)
        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as e:
            print(f"error: {e}", flush=True)
            return 1
        print("@@RESULT " + json.dumps(res), flush=True)
        return 0

    names = a.names or [t["name"] for t in motion.list_templates()]
    if a.missing:
        names = [n for n in names if not has_preview(n)]
    if not names:
        print("all templates have previews")
        return 0
    fails = 0
    for i, n in enumerate(names, 1):
        print(f"[{i}/{len(names)}] {n} ...", flush=True)
        try:
            r = make(n, force=a.force)
            if r["skipped"]:
                print(f"[preview] {n}: up to date", flush=True)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep going through the other templates
            fails += 1
            print(f"[preview] {n}: FAILED: {e}", flush=True)
    print(f"done: {len(names) - fails} ok, {fails} failed", flush=True)
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

            "poster": MP.rel_url(p["jpg"]) if p["jpg"].exists() else None,
            "preview": f"motion/previews/{name}.jpg" if p["jpg"].exists() else None}   # Brand page compat


@app.get("/api/motion")
def motion_templates():
    """Every template under studio/motion/templates (discovered on each call), with previews if made."""
    from . import motion as M
    out = []
    tdir = M.TEMPLATES
    for d in sorted(tdir.iterdir()) if tdir.exists() else []:
        if not (d / "template.json").exists():
            continue
        try:
            out.append(_motion_template_out(M._manifest(d.name)))
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            out.append({"name": d.name, "description": f"(template.json unreadable: {e})", "vars": [],
                        "orientations": [], "broken": True})
    return {"templates": out, "missing_previews": [t["name"] for t in out
                                                   if not t.get("preview_mp4") and not t.get("broken")]}


class MotionRender(BaseModel):
    name: str
    vars: dict = {}
    orientation: str = "landscape"
    preview: bool = True
    duration: float | None = None


@app.post("/api/motion/render")
def motion_render(body: MotionRender):
    from . import motion as M
    try:
        m = M._manifest(body.name)
        M.resolve_vars(body.name, {k: v for k, v in body.vars.items() if k != "opaque"})
    except ValueError as e:
        raise HTTPException(400, str(e)) from None
    if body.orientation not in m.get("orientations", []):
        raise HTTPException(400, f"'{body.name}' has no {body.orientation} version")
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "mcstudio.motion_previews", "--render", body.name,
           "--vars", json.dumps({k: v for k, v in body.vars.items() if k != "opaque"}),
           "--orientation", body.orientation]
    if body.preview:
        cmd.append("--preview")
    if body.duration:
        cmd += ["--duration", str(body.duration)]
    job = Job("_motion", f"motion:{body.name}", cmd, STUDIO)
    JOBS[job.id] = job
    return job.public()


class MotionPreviews(BaseModel):
    names: list[str] = []
    force: bool = False


@app.post("/api/motion/previews")
def motion_previews(body: MotionPreviews | None = None):
    """Regenerate previews: the given names, else only templates missing one."""
    body = body or MotionPreviews()
    if any(j.slug == "_motion" and j.stage == "motion-previews" and j.status == "running" for j in JOBS.values()):
        raise HTTPException(409, "previews are already being generated")
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "mcstudio.motion_previews", *body.names]
    if not body.names:
        cmd.append("--missing")
    if body.force:
        cmd.append("--force")
    job = Job("_motion", "motion-previews", cmd, STUDIO)
    JOBS[job.id] = job
    return job.public()

- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID ("name@team") or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status

input.message:
The Motion graphics page is built and tested end to end on a test server (port 8798, now stopped). **Your server on port 8765 needs a restart** before it will serve the new endpoints. I didn't touch it.

**1. Previews: `studio/mcstudio/motion_previews.py`**
- `make(name, force=False)` renders the template in preview mode (landscape, default vars) through `motion.render`. It puts the alpha .mov over a gameplay still and writes `studio/motion/previews/<name>.mp4` (h264, 960x540, 30fps, with a 0.5s transparent tail so it loops cleanly), a `<name>.jpg` mid-frame poster, and a `<name>.json` that records the source .mov name.
- It only rebuilds when `motion.render` returns a different .mov, i.e. when the template, the shared files or brand.json changed.
- The gameplay still is pulled once from test-clip-02's game recording at 40% of its length (`_bg_landscape.jpg`; `_bg_vertical.jpg` is a centre crop). Other projects' game files come next, and a dark checkerboard is the last fallback.
- The background image is looped with ffmpeg's `loop` filter, not `-loop 1`, to avoid the ffmpeg 9 stall noted in CLAUDE.md.
- CLI: `uv run python -m mcstudio.motion_previews [names...] [--missing] [--force]`.
- The same module has a `--render NAME --vars JSON --orientation O [--preview] [--duration S]` mode that the UI's render jobs use. It renders, makes a browser-playable mp4 in `motion/previews/renders/<mov-stem>.mp4`, and prints a result line the server reads.
- I ran it for every template. Templates are found from the folder each time, so the 4 that appeared while I worked (advancement_toast, block_break_wipe, callout_arrow, speech_bubble) were picked up automatically. All 16 have previews and none failed.

**2. API in `studio/mcstudio/server.py`**
- **GET `/api/motion`** returns `{templates, missing_previews}`. Each template has name, description, kind, duration, stretchable, min_duration, cut_at, orientations, preview_mp4 and poster URLs, and vars as `{key, type, label, default, brand, options, min, max, step}`.
  - Defaults are resolved, including brand colours and names.
  - `opaque` is left out of the vars.
  - Options come from `options`/`enum` if a template defines them. Otherwise they're read from labels like `"Block style: color | stone | ..."`, which is how pixel_wipe's style gets a dropdown.
  - A template.json that can't be read shows up as "broken" instead of breaking the page.
- **POST `/api/motion/render`** takes `{name, vars, orientation, preview, duration?}`. It checks the vars first (an unknown var returns 400), then starts a `Job` (slug `_motion`). The `Job` class now has a `result` field. A finished job's result includes `mov` (relative path for the editor), `mov_url`, `mp4_url` (viewable over gameplay), the resolved vars and the size.
- **POST `/api/motion/previews`** takes `{names?, force?}`. With no names it only does templates missing a preview, and it refuses to start a second preview job while one is running.
- All outputs are served under `/media/studio/motion/...`.

**3. UI (`ui/index.html`, `ui/app.js`, `ui/style.css`)**
- New nav item "Motion graphics" at `#/motion`.
- Template cards show the poster and play the preview mp4 on hover, muted and looping. Each card has the name, description, duration (with a "+" if stretchable), a kind badge and 16:9 / 9:16 badges.
- Clicking a card opens the drawer with the big looping preview and a form built from the template's vars: text inputs, number inputs, colour picker plus hex field, checkboxes, and dropdowns. Stretchable templates also get a duration field.
- The drawer also has a landscape/vertical toggle, a "Quick preview (540p30)" checkbox (on by default), Reset, and Render.
- Render shows a live log, then plays the result, offers "Download .mov (alpha)" and "Copy path", and fills in the EDL snippet. The snippet only includes vars you changed from the defaults, e.g. `{"type":"motion","template":"pixel_wipe","vars":{"style":"stone"},"seg":"<segment id>","rel":0}`. One small difference from your example: `rel` prints as `0`, not `0.0` (it's the same number in JSON).
- Form values are remembered per template in localStorage.
- "↻ Regenerate previews" runs the missing-preview job, shows progress, and reloads the grid.
- The Jobs page now sends `_motion` and `_library` jobs to their own pages instead of a broken project link.

**4. Brand page:** the motion section is now one card with the template count and an "Open motion graphics →" button.

**Checks**
- `node --check ui/app.js` passes.
- curl tests:
  - `/api/motion` listed every template.
  - The preview job built the 2 that were missing at the time.
  - A vertical counter render with custom vars finished in about 18s and returned working `mov_url` and `mp4_url`.
  - A bad var returned 400.
- In the browser pane:
  - Cards rendered and the hover video played.
  - The drawer form showed the pixel_wipe style dropdown.
  - A Render from the UI finished in 9s, played the result, and showed the download link and the updated snippet.
  - The Brand page link was there.

Other agents are still editing templates (mc_title and speech_bubble were re-made on my last pass because their files had changed). Running the CLI or clicking the button picks up any further changes.
